check: Regeneration check: are the external-benchmark replies reproducible at temperature 0?
expected: replies re-generated at temperature 0 reproduce the stored replies byte for byte
summary: Re-decoding at temperature 0 under batched vLLM is not byte-stable: 8,407 of 26,880 replayed items (31.3%) differ textually from the stored replies. Verdicts are stable: for Granite-3.3-2B, regraded end to end in all five versions, 2.56% of items change pass/fail status and the pooled Base pass rate moves by 0.06 pp. Reported differences are robust to this instability; byte reproducibility is not claimed.
why_it_happens: Batch composition varies between runs, which changes floating-point reduction order, which perturbs logits in the last decimal and occasionally flips an argmax. This is a known property of batched inference engines, not a defect in this study's harness.

known_limitations: Divergence is not a property of the model alone: within Granite-3.3-2B the five versions span 48.5%-64.8% and the Base version is the lowest, so version and model are confounded in any cross-cell comparison of divergence rates.
Verdict stability rests on one model: the other four cells were replayed (text) but not regraded.
